patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: The parents report no known allergies, normal birth and developmental history for the child.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies fever, rash, or recent illnesses.

questions: Does the child have fever or refuse to bear weight because of pain in that right knee?
Does the child have any redness, warmth, or limited range of motion in the right knee?
How long has the right knee swelling been present, and has it been getting progressively larger?
What does the scalp lesion look like (e.g., size, color, whether it’s scaly/itchy, draining pus, or is it a firm lump)?
Is the scalp lump attached to the skin (or is it freely movable under the skin) and approximately how big is it in centimeters?
Does the firm scalp lump have a central pore/scab or any ulceration, and is it tender to touch?
Does the scalp lump have a central “punctum” (a small dark dot/hole) or a crusty keratin plug when you look closely at it?
“Can you describe the scalp lesion more specifically—does it have a central dimple/punctum or a thick keratin plug?”
Has the scalp lump increased in size or changed appearance since you first noticed it?
Does the scalp lump have any overlying scaling or crust (e.g., thick yellow/white keratin) on its surface?
answers: Patient: I don’t have fever, and I’m not having any pain that makes it hard to bear weight. I’m here mainly for a routine checkup, and I’ve noticed a lesion on my scalp.
“No, I don’t have any right-knee redness or warmth, and my range of motion feels normal. I’m really only concerned about the lesion I noticed on my scalp during this routine checkup.”

“No, I don’t have right-knee swelling at all—so it hasn’t been changing or getting bigger. I’m mainly focused on the lesion on my scalp, which I first noticed recently, but I’m not sure exactly how long it’s been there before I saw it.”

“Well, I noticed it recently but I haven’t measured it—it's on my scalp and it looks like a firm lump. It’s not draining pus, I haven’t seen any redness around it, and I’m not particularly bothered by itching, scale, or anything wet.”
“It feels like it’s attached to the skin and doesn’t move much when I touch it. I haven’t measured it with a ruler, but it seems about a couple of centimeters across.”
“I haven’t noticed any central pore, scab, or any ulceration on it, and it isn’t tender when I press on it. It just feels like a firm lump attached to the skin.”
“I haven’t seen any small dark dot, hole, or crusty keratin plug—just a firm lump attached to the skin. When I look closely, it doesn’t seem to have any central punctum.”
“It doesn’t have a central dimple, punctum, or thick keratin plug—just a firm lump attached to the skin on my scalp. I haven’t noticed any ulceration or drainage either.”
“No, it hasn’t increased in size or changed much in appearance since I first noticed it—it's basically stayed the same. I’m mainly here because it’s a new firm lump on my scalp that I want checked.”
“No, I haven’t noticed any thick yellow or white crust, scaling, or anything like that on the surface—just a firm lump that feels attached to my scalp.”
